cues.en: Please welcome Darius Kazemi. Hi, everybody. Yeah, there we go. It's an honor to be here today talking to my fellow creators. I'm really excited to tell you the story of how I got to where I am today. Ever since I was a child, I wanted to win the lottery. I think it started when I would visit my grandmother as a child. Every night at 6 o'clock,
cues.zh: 让我们欢迎 Darius Kazemi。大家好。好的，这就对了。今天很荣幸能来到这里，与各位创作者同行交流。我非常激动能与大家分享我是如何走到今天的。打小起，我就一直想中彩票。我想这一切大概始于小时候去外婆家的那些日子。每天晚上6点，

cues.en: We watched action news on WPVI Channel 6. We weren't really watching for the news. At 6.59, the Pennsylvania lottery daily number was drawn, and we'd hold our breath until that first little ping pong ball came out of its pneumatic tube. She never won, but it gave me hope, and it was my strongest memory of the strongest woman I knew. Needless to say, the lottery soon became an all-consuming passion.
cues.zh: 我们都会收看 WPVI 6频道的《Action News》。其实我们并不是真为了看新闻。6点59分，宾夕法尼亚州的每日彩票就会开奖，我们会屏住呼吸，直到第一个小乒乓球从气动管里弹出来。她从来没中过，但那给了我希望，也是关于我所认识的最坚强的女性的最深刻记忆。不用说，彩票很快成了我全部的热情所在。

cues.en: In every spare moment I had, I doodle numbers in notebooks, the margins of pages, wherever else I could think. This is my life. That passion stayed with me through my teen years and into my college days. By the time I hit my early 20s, I set aside every day to buy a lottery ticket and improve my craft. Although I didn't see it as improving my craft,
cues.zh: 只要一有空闲，我就会在笔记本上、书页的空白处，以及任何我能想到的地方涂写数字。这就是我的生活。这份热情伴随我度过了少年时代，一直持续到大学。到了20出头的时候，我每天都会留出时间去买彩票，精进我的技艺。尽管当时我并没把它看作是在精进技艺，

cues.en: Really, what the lottery had become for me was a way of processing what happened to me every day. When I got into a fender bender, I used the numbers from the other guy's license plate. If I met a girl at a bar, I'd incorporate her phone number into my work. It's very important to me. There was a period of my life where I was going through some awful medical problems, and I played the numbers that I found around me every day at the hospital, and it took an awful...
cues.zh: 实际上，彩票对我来说已经变成了一种消化每天发生的事情的方式。如果碰上了小车祸，我就会用对方车牌上的数字。如果我在酒吧遇到一个女孩，我就会把她的电话号码融入到我的作品中。这对我来说意义重大。我人生中有一段时期饱受糟糕的健康问题困扰，我就用每天在医院周围看到的数字去买彩票，这把一段可怕的……

cues.en: isolating ordeal, and provided me a way to share it with my friends and family. I didn't have a lot of success as a lottery player at first, but I kept doing it. And more importantly, I started sharing my experience on the Internet with my lottery blog. It began as a daily journal of the numbers that I played, but it became so much more over time. Not only, a great blog, not only did this experiment
cues.zh: 孤立无援的煎熬，变成了一种能让我与亲朋好友分享的方式。起初，作为一个彩民我并没取得什么成功，但我一直坚持着。更重要的是，我开始在互联网上通过我的彩票博客分享我的经历。它一开始只是我投注数字的日常记录，但随着时间推移，它承载的意义远不止于此。不仅是一个很棒的博客，不仅这个尝试

cues.en: keep me active as a content creator. But it also very slowly built up a wonderful community. A community of lottery players I still talk to this very day. The most freeing thing about this blog was the feedback loop between myself and my small group of dedicated fans. I'd start to get feedback from them. Here's one great example. I'll always remember this. My mom's birthday was coming up.
cues.zh: 让我保持着内容创作者的活力。而且它还慢慢建立起了一个美好的社区。一个我至今仍在交流的彩民社区。这个博客最让我感到自由的，是我与少数忠实粉丝之间的反馈闭环。我开始收到他们的反馈。这里有个绝佳的例子。我永远都会记得这个。当时我妈妈的生日快到了。

cues.en: So I played her birthday, you know, as you do. And one of my fans commented on the post for that day and said, hey, I know your mom's birthday is coming up, but have you considered mixing it up and trying your dad's birthday? And you know, in all my years of playing the lottery, I had never, not even once, considered playing my dad's birthday on my mom's birthday.
cues.zh: 所以我就买了她的生日数字，你知道的，大家都会这么做。我的一位粉丝在那天的帖子下评论说，嘿，我知道你妈妈的生日快到了，但你有没有考虑过换换花样，试试你爸爸的生日？你知道吗，在我买彩票的这么多年里，我从来没有，哪怕一次，考虑过在我妈妈生日那天买我爸爸的生日。

cues.en: And so we ended up with this brilliant community of lateral thinkers supporting ourselves in our lottery endeavors. At the time, none of us had made it big. You know, we weren't well-known lottery players. None of us really knew what we were doing, but that freed us. I was so inspired by this community that I wanted to devote myself to it.
cues.zh: 于是我们最终有了这个由横向思维者组成的出色社区，大家互相支持彼此的彩票事业。当时我们谁都没做大。我们不是什么知名彩票玩家。其实没人真懂自己在干嘛，但这反而解放了我们。这个社区太激励我了，我想投入其中。

cues.en: full time. So I gathered up some of my closest friends from that community, and I quit my day job as executive vice president of portfolio management services at Lehman Brothers. And I used some of that nest egg that I had squirreled away. I bought a little loft on the Upper East Side of Manhattan, and it became known as simply the lottery collective.
cues.zh: 而且是全职投入。于是，我召集了社区里一些最亲近的朋友，辞掉了我在雷曼兄弟的工作——投资组合管理服务执行副总裁。我还动用了自己攒下的一部分积蓄，在曼哈顿上东区买了个小阁楼，后来这里就被简单称作彩票集体。

cues.en: I worked at the Lottery Collective for a few years. It was a one in a million experience. I was surrounded by the best and the brightest, and all of us were working hard on lottery permutations, studying the techniques of our heroes, and trying to live as simply as possible. And then I got my big break. Now...
cues.zh: 我在彩票集体工作了几年。那是千载难逢的经历。身边都是最优秀、最聪明的人，我们都在努力研究彩票排列组合，学习偶像们的技巧，并尽量简单生活。然后我迎来了重大转机。现在……

cues.en: I'm sure most of you are familiar with that. My win is a story that's been repeated all over the place, and I'm not going to bore you with that today. This is a special crowd of fellow creators, and I owe you something a little different. A lot of people in the creative world don't like to talk numbers. Like it's a dirty secret that we're not supposed to acknowledge. And I totally understand. What will people think if you share your numbers? What will they do? But while I understand,
cues.zh: 我肯定大多数人都熟悉那个。我的中奖故事到处都被反复讲，今天就不烦你们了。这是一群特别的同行创作者，我该给你们讲点不一样的。创意界很多人不喜欢谈数字。好像这是我们不该承认的见不得人的秘密。我完全理解。你要是分享自己的数字，别人会怎么想？他们会怎么做？但我虽然理解，

cues.en: this attitude. I think it's wrong. I think it's incumbent upon me as a successful creator to share my numbers because I could not have gotten here without my blog community, the lottery collective, and the giants of yesteryear on whose shoulders I stand. So here we go. These are my numbers. Thank you. You're the first to see them. And as you can see, there are an awful lot of nines.
cues.zh: 这种态度，但我觉得这是错的。作为成功的创作者，我有责任分享我的数字，因为没有我的博客社区、彩票集体，以及那些我站在其肩膀上的昔日巨人，我走不到这里。那开始吧。这些就是我的数字。谢谢。你们是第一批看到的人。如你们所见，里面有非常多的 9。

cues.en: and a surprising number of threes. Now, you might not notice this at first, but nine is three times three. Now, I'm not an economist or a mathematician, so take what I'm about to say here with a grain of salt. But I think this means that there's room out there for niche numbers. And I just want to be totally clear.
cues.zh: 还有多得惊人的 3。你可能一开始没注意，但 9 是 3 的三倍。我不是经济学家也不是数学家，所以接下来说的话你们姑且听听。但我觉得这意味着，小众数字还有空间。我想说得非常清楚。

cues.en: I'm not saying that you should play a bunch of nines and threes the next time you play the lottery. That would be absurd. Nines and threes worked for me, and they worked for me once, and they're probably not going to work for you. But what I am saying is get a little wild. Stretch a little. Try some eights or a lot of sevens. Those! What my lottery ticket shows.
cues.zh: 我不是说下次买彩票时，你该买一堆 9 和 3。那太荒唐了。9 和 3 对我有效，而且只对我有效过一次，它们大概率不会对你有用。但我想说的是，稍微放飞一点。大胆扩展一下。试试一些 8，或者来很多 7。就那些！我的彩票上显示的就是这些。

cues.en: is that there's room in this world for all kinds of numbers, as long as you build a community around it. For the five years that I was full-time running my blog and participating in the lottery collective, I spent an average of $2 a day on lottery tickets. I ended up spending about three grand over the course of the experience. And as you can see, that paid off. Thank you.
cues.zh: 那就是这个世界上容得下各种各样的数字，只要你围绕它建立起一个社群。在我全职写博客并参与彩票互助团体的五年里，我平均每天花 2 美元买彩票。整个过程下来，我大概花了三千美元。而如大家所见，这笔投资得到了回报。谢谢。

cues.en: But what this really shows is the value of community. I had a small community of about a thousand regular posters and fans on my blog. To a big advertising company, each one of those people is worth about two cents. But if you take the success of this project at $140 million and divide it by those thousand community members,
cues.zh: 但这真正展现的，其实是社群的价值。我的博客上有一个大约一千名常客和粉丝组成的小社群。对大型广告公司来说，这里的每个人大概就值两分钱。但如果你把这个项目 1.4 亿美元的收益平摊到这一千名社群成员头上，

cues.en: It turns out that each of my fans is worth $140,000. This is the value of community. So to sum things up, I know what I was doing. I didn't. But I kept buying lottery tickets anyway and playing numbers that just appealed to me. But in addition to making things that I liked, I reached out to fellow lottery number creators and general fans of the lottery, and I ended up building a community. And so in the end, I learned the real formula for success.
cues.zh: 算下来，我的每个粉丝就价值 14 万美元。这就是社群的价值。总而言之，我知道自己在做什么吗？完全不知道。但我还是不停地买彩票，选那些合我眼缘的数字。除了做自己喜欢的东西，我还去结识了其他选号创作者和普通彩民，最终建立了一个社群。就这样，我参透了成功的真正秘诀。

cues.en: Keep buying those lottery tickets. Keep making those connections, and you'll win the lottery, too. Thank you. Now, okay, so that... Thanks. So that was how I won the lottery, or as I like to call it, every talk ever given by a successful creative person.
cues.zh: 继续买彩票吧。继续去建立连接，你也一样能中大奖。谢谢。好了，刚才这段……谢谢。刚才那就是我是怎么中彩票的，或者按我的说法，这是“所有成功创意人士演讲的标准套路”。

cues.en: There are a few key things that I wanted to draw attention to. I was thinking of dropping the mic, but then, you know, that seemed a little, I don't know, I was just gonna go over this. I actually wrote this talk on the flight home from XOXO last year, and I was trying to find a venue as cool as XOXO with like the same demographics and stuff, and then Andy was like, do you wanna speak next year? And I was like, I already have a talk written. But it came in under, so you get this part.
cues.zh: 这里有几个关键点我想重点聊聊。我刚才本来想帅气地扔话筒下台，但又觉得有点……算了，我还是把这部分讲完吧。其实这场演讲是我去年坐飞机离开 XOXO 时写好的，我当时到处找跟 XOXO 一样酷、受众也类似的场子，结果 Andy 就问我：明年想来做个演讲吗？我立刻说：我连稿子都写好了。不过刚才讲得有点快，所以你们就赚到了这一段。

cues.en: The first thing I want to talk about is this lottery metaphor itself. I believe that beyond a certain threshold of work that you put into your projects, success is entirely out of your hands. Conceiving of a creative project and building it, that's buying a lottery ticket. That's the hard work and don't be a jerk kind of like, okay, you've bought your lottery ticket, great. I make what I like to call weird internet stuff.
cues.zh: 我想聊的第一点，就是这个彩票的比喻本身。我认为，在你在项目上投入的心血超过某个阈值之后，成功与否就完全不是你能掌控的了。构思一个创意项目并把它做出来，其实就是在买一张彩票。努力做好、别犯浑，这就好比“行了，你已经买了彩票，挺好”。我平时做的，是我称之为“奇奇怪怪的互联网玩意儿”的东西，

cues.en: which I've recently come to accept is internet art. And I just want to show you some examples of projects that I made which had good public receptions and projects that I made that basically nobody cared about at all. Here's miraculous pics. If you're familiar with those...
cues.zh: 不过我最近已经接受了它其实算“网络艺术”。我只想给大家看几个我做的项目，有些反响很好，有些则根本无人问津。比如这个 miraculous pics。如果你知道的话……

cues.en: scummy Twitter accounts like that that just like get zillions of followers and they post sort of like Amazing pics or beautiful pics or whatever and they always get the attributions wrong or they don't attribute or it's like This is a picture of Hawaii and it's like no that's a picture of Bali or whatever But they get millions of retweets because they're beautiful pictures and that sort of thing and so and so I was like well I hate these things and so I'm gonna make one that's just really wrong and so this just this this is a bot that just
cues.zh: 像那种很烂的 Twitter 账号，随随便便就涨几百万粉丝，发些特别惊艳或漂亮的照片之类的，还总是把出处标错，或者干脆不标，比如说“这是夏威夷的照片”，结果根本不是，那是巴厘岛之类的。但它们就因为照片漂亮之类的原因，能拿到几百万次转发。所以我就想，好吧，我讨厌这些东西，那我要做一个完全乱来的。所以这个，这就是一个机器人，它只是

cues.en: grabs random captions from those scummy accounts, and then does a Google image search and just grabs something at random and puts them on top of each other. So we get, this is a new level of cuteness, or how to kiss a boy, or why do girls text nude pics? Here's why. And I thought of this project on the way home from work. I got home. I made it. I pushed it online. I had dinner.
cues.zh: 从那些垃圾账号随机抓取配文，然后做 Google 图片搜索，随便抓一张图，再把图和配文叠在一起。于是我们就得到“这是可爱的新境界”，或者“怎么亲一个男孩”，或者“为什么女生会发裸照？原因如下”。这个项目是我下班回家路上想到的。我到家，把它做出来，发布上线，然后吃了晚饭。

cues.en: It took like an hour because it was like two API calls to get the data and then a third API call to put it on Twitter. It was pretty easy. And this got actually a fair amount of traction.
cues.zh: 大概花了一个小时，因为就是两次 API 调用拿数据，再来第三次 API 调用发到 Twitter 上。挺简单的。而这个项目居然还获得了不少关注。

cues.en: TLDR wrote an article about this. It got some traction. Sometimes when I talk to people, they say, oh, miraculous pics is like my favorite Twitter bot. And I'm like, that's cool, that's awesome, I really like to hear that. Here's another one that took about the same amount of work. It's called Alt-Universe Prompts. Get a load of that one. And what this is, is it goes to, it attempts to create crossover.
cues.zh: TLDR 写了一篇关于它的文章。它获得了一些关注。有时候我跟人聊天，他们会说，哦，Miraculous Pics 简直是我最喜欢的 Twitter 机器人。我就想，真酷，太棒了，我很爱听这个。还有一个项目，花的工作量差不多。它叫 Alt-Universe Prompts。来看看这个。它做的事情是，它会去，它试图创作跨界。

cues.en: alternate universe scenario fan fiction prompts actually pulled from Archive of Our Own, which was mentioned earlier today. And it just grabs two characters and then it goes to Twitter and it finds someone saying something aspirational, like, I wish I was in bed right now. And then it just snips that off and then puts it next to two characters and drops a heart on it and it creates these prompts. And so we get stuff like this, we get...
cues.zh: 平行宇宙设定的同人小说提示词，实际上是从 Archive of Our Own 抓来的，今天早些时候提到过这个网站。它就是抓两个角色，然后去 Twitter 上找有人说一些向往的话，比如“我希望我现在正躺在床上”。然后它就把这句话剪下来，放到两个角色旁边，再在上面加个爱心，生成这些提示词。于是我们就得到这样的东西，我们会得到……

cues.en: Queen Perkins and the 11th doctor in a basement. That's not going to end well for the doctor. And cigarettes smoking. That one got some faves. But mostly they're just a few people who care about this one quite deeply. But it's like the same four people who really like it all the time.
cues.zh: Queen Perkins 和第十一任博士在地下室里。这对博士来说不会有好结局。还有抽烟。那条拿到了一些点赞。但大多数时候，就只有少数几个人特别在意这个。而且总是同样那四个人一直很喜欢它。

cues.en: So yeah, I like this one as much as I like the last one. And in fact, I put more work into this. But I never know when I launch something if it's going to get picked up and really popular or what. Here's another one that I really like and makes me laugh every time it comes across my Twitter feed.
cues.zh: 所以是的，我喜欢这个，和喜欢上一个一样。事实上，我在这个上花了更多功夫。但我永远不知道，当我发布一个东西时，它会不会被大家接受、变得很流行，还是怎样。还有一个我真的很喜欢，每次它出现在我的 Twitter 信息流里，都会让我笑。

cues.en: This is like that champagne for my real friends, real pain for my sham friends. This actually uses Wordnik, so thank you, Aaron. Wordnik gives you bigrams, so you can give it a word, and then it'll give you another word that's sort of likely to appear next to it. So, naked examination for my closer friends, closer examination for my naked friends. Female president for my leftist friends, leftist president for my female friends.
cues.zh: 这就像那句“给真朋友香槟，给假朋友真痛”。这个项目其实用了 Wordnik，谢谢 Aaron。Wordnik 能提供二元语法词对，你给它一个词，它就会返回一个很可能出现在它后面的词。所以就有了“给我亲近的朋友赤裸的审视，给我赤裸的朋友更近的审视”。“给我的左派朋友一位女总统，给我的女性朋友一位左派总统”。

cues.en: and Real Housewives for my Desperate Dogs, Desperate Housewives for my Real Dogs. I really like this one and no one cares. No one cares. And then my most popular Twitter bot came from me noticing a really lazy style of joke on Twitter that I saw repeated over and over and over again.
cues.zh: 还有“给我绝望的狗看《真实主妇》，给我真正的狗看《绝望主妇》”。我超喜欢这个，但根本没人理。根本没人理。后来我做了一个最火的 Twitter 机器人，灵感来自我在 Twitter 上看到的一种被反复套用的极度偷懒的段子套路。

cues.en: where like two popular, two big news items would happen, and then like people would tell the joke where they mix them up. So like, oh, there's an Apple keynote, and the next Batman was announced, so let's talk about, you know, some Batman Apple joke, right? So I built two headlines, which does stuff like this. And that's 13 Kuwaiti aid-loaded trucks enter NASCAR.
cues.zh: 就是每当有两条大新闻发生时，大家就会讲那种把两者混在一起的段子。比如，哦，苹果开了发布会，同时新一部《蝙蝠侠》公布了，大家就开始讲什么蝙蝠侠和苹果结合的烂梗，对吧？所以我做了 Two Headlines，效果就像这样：比如“13辆满载科威特援助物资的卡车驶入 NASCAR 赛道”。

cues.en: This one is particularly clever, so I picked a good example. But all it does is it goes to Google News. It picks headlines from two different categories. Google News does a little callout of the main subject of a given headline. And I just find the subject in one, grab a subject from somewhere else, and just swap it in. So this one must have swapped Iraq for NASCAR or something. Google to buy Syria in $3.2 billion deal.
cues.zh: 这条特别绝，所以我特意挑了这个好例子。但它的原理其实就是抓取 Google News。从两个不同类别里各挑一条头条。Google News 会标出一条新闻的主语。我只要找出一条里的主语，再从另一条里抓个主语直接替换掉。所以这条肯定是把“伊拉克”换成了“NASCAR”之类的。“Google 拟斥资32亿美元收购叙利亚”。

cues.en: China to remain an American company so And I really like this one just as much as I liked all the other ones and this one did get fairly popular And so, you know, I just like this it I don't know what happens to these things after I put them out in the wild I buy a lot of lottery tickets
cues.zh: “中国仍将是一家美国公司”等等。其实我和喜欢其他作品一样喜欢这个，而且这个确实挺火。所以你看，我就是喜欢这个过程。东西放出去之后会怎样我根本控制不了，我只是买了很多彩票。

cues.en: This is a list of every creative project I've released since January 2013, representing 21 months of part-time noodling around with art and technology. These are creative projects that I've put anywhere from one to 200 hours of work into. And what I've learned from doing over 100 projects in the last couple of years is that beyond a certain level of effort, there's basically no correlation between the amount of work you put into something and how successful it is, at least for me.
cues.zh: 这是我自2013年1月以来发布的所有创意项目清单，代表了我21个月里利用业余时间在艺术和技术上的摸索。这些创意项目，我每个都投入了1到200小时不等的心血。过去几年做了100多个项目后，我明白了一点：一旦超过某个努力门槛，你的投入程度和它的成功之间，基本上没有任何关联，至少对我来说是这样。

cues.en: These are projects that I've got significant press recognition for. That's nine out of 112 projects. That actually lines up with the Song-A-Day talk from yesterday pretty nicely. And I believe that once you've made your thing and bought your lottery ticket, everything that comes after that in terms of recognition of what you've done, whether it's good reviews or money or success, is up to some kind of combination of luck and prior privilege. And you might ask,
cues.zh: 这些是我获得了大量媒体报道的项目。112个项目里只有9个。这跟昨天那个“每天写一首歌”的演讲还挺契合的。我相信，一旦你把东西做出来并买了彩票，之后所有关于认可的事情——不管是好评、金钱还是成功——都取决于某种运气和既有特权的结合。你可能会问，

cues.en: What about marketing? What about PR? What about knowing your audience? What about making your thing better? Doesn't that help? To me, yes, it does. And that's kind of just buying the lottery ticket. For me, that's all part of buying the lottery ticket, depending on the scope of the project you're releasing. Let's talk about the coolest. Just for a bit. This is the most successful Kickstarter ever.
cues.zh: 营销呢？公关呢？了解受众呢？把东西做得更好呢？这些没用吗？在我看来，有用。但这本身也不过是在买彩票罢了。对我来说，取决于你发布项目的规模，这些全都是买彩票的一部分。我们来聊聊 Coolest。就聊一会儿。这是 Kickstarter 史上最成功的项目。

cues.en: $13 million for a cooler with some extra appliances attached to it. This is not a high-end design product like the PenType A or a fancy watch. It didn't have a slick marketing campaign. Its aesthetic is cheesy like an infomercial and not in an ironic way. So why did it succeed? Well, you might say people clearly want a party in a box supercooler. It must have been the strength of the idea that carried it through.
cues.zh: 一台附带了几个额外电器的冷藏箱，卖了1300万美元。它不是PenType A或高级手表那样的高端设计产品。它没有花哨的营销活动。它的美学像电视购物广告一样俗气，而且不是反讽式的俗气。那它为什么成功？你可能会说，人们显然想要一台“箱装派对”超级冷藏箱。一定是这个点子的力量让它成功了。

cues.en: Except if you look at the Kickstarter profile of the guy who invented it, you'll find one other project that he tried to launch on Kickstarter that failed, and that project was the exact same thing six months earlier. Same thing. The design's a little clunkier, but it's the same idea with complete feature parity, plus even more features like a grill for some reason. So what changed? The inventor claims it's because people like coolers more in the summer than in the winter.
cues.zh: 只不过，如果你看看发明者的Kickstarter个人资料页，会发现他还试过在Kickstarter上发起另一个项目，但失败了；而那个项目就是六个月前一模一样的东西。一模一样。设计更笨重一点，但想法相同、功能完全对等，甚至不知为何还多了个烤架之类的功能。那变化在哪？发明者声称，是因为人们在夏天比冬天更喜欢冷藏箱。

cues.en: Okay, does that account for $13 million worth of difference in the value of your idea and all that work you put in? He also said this because he had backers who carried over from the last one, all 279 of them. Now that's some community that's worth something right there. And he said the video was better, but $13 million better? Did he pay Martin Scorsese like $6 million to produce his Kickstarter video?
cues.zh: 好吧，这能解释你的点子和投入的所有工作，价值上出现1300万美元的差距吗？他还说，是因为上一次项目有支持者延续过来，总共279人。这可就是一个真有价值的社群了。他还说视频更好了，但能好出1300万美元？他难道付了Martin Scorsese大约600万美元来制作Kickstarter视频吗？

cues.en: I don't know, perhaps an orange trapezoid is $13 million better than a gray rectangle. Regardless, I believe the inventor when he says it could have been a mix of any one of those reasons. I also think it could have been due to the single right person, maybe a TV producer at NBC, seeing a tweet about it because their flight was running late and they glanced at their phone. Maybe a butterfly flapped its wings in the rainforest.
cues.zh: 我不知道，也许一个橙色梯形就是比灰色矩形好出1300万美元。无论如何，我相信发明者说的：原因可能是上述任一原因的组合。我也认为，可能只是因为一个恰好对的人——也许是NBC的一位电视制片人——因为航班延误，瞥了一眼手机，看到了相关推文。也许是一只蝴蝶在雨林里扇动了翅膀。

cues.en: Maybe it's because billions of years ago, two distant galaxies collided and the resulting conflagration fused particles into never-before-seen elements that got violently ejected into our part of the universe, setting in motion a chain of mysterious and unthinkable cosmic events that eventually resulted in the coolest. This may seem like fatalism. In a sense, it is.
cues.zh: 也许是因为数十亿年前，两个遥远星系相撞，产生的大火把粒子聚变成前所未见的元素，这些元素被猛烈抛射到宇宙中我们所在的区域，启动了一连串神秘而不可想象的宇宙事件，最终造就了这台“最酷”的冷藏箱。这看起来像宿命论。某种意义上，确实是。

cues.en: There's not much that you can control about your creative success once you've actually made the thing. And in a sense, there are two kinds of creative advice that I think you can get from creative people. The first is how to buy more lottery tickets. And the second is how to win the lottery. And I think the former can be extremely useful. And I think the latter is nonsense. And that's all I got. Thank you.
cues.zh: 一旦你真的把东西做出来，你能控制的创作成功因素就不多了。某种意义上，我认为你能从有创造力的人那里得到两种创作建议。第一种是如何买更多彩票。第二种是如何中彩票。我认为前者可能极其有用。而我认为后者是胡说八道。这就是我要说的。谢谢。
